paragraphs: R’ Yuda Gozaria reported in the name of R’ Acha, as cited in Jerusalem Talmud Rosh Hashanah 3:9. At the end of Jerusalem Talmud Megillah 1:5, the text gives the compressed wording “Rabbi Yaakov bar Acha and Rabbi Yudan Gezuri, Rabbi Simon in the name of Rabbi Yehoshua ben Levi.”

notes.text: The consulted Megillah paragraph spells out Rabbi Yehoshua ben Levi, not Resh Lakish. It preserves the compressed Yaakov/Yudan/Simon chain, whose intermediate connections remain unresolved here.

The saved Machon HaYerushalmi/Buch2017 Ohr LaYesharim scalar was read only in the complete connected rebuttal/transmission paragraph (offsets7621–8959), not the entire12296-character commentary. It explicitly interprets Yaakov bar Acha → Yudan Gezuri → Simon → Yehoshua ben Levi, writing בשם (ו) in its explanation and tentatively associating Gezuri with Gezer. That is the modern commentator’s interpretation, not a manuscript correction or admitted identity/place. The final-chain full Rabbi titles are explicit in that connected quotation; the separate Rosh Hashanah heading/Acha occurrences remain R' without title transfer. Hyman’s Gozaria/Gezuri forms and compressed chain remain.

The consulted Rosh Hashanah 3:9 has Rabbi Yehudah Gozaria reporting in Rabbi Acha’s name. Megillah 1:5:7 has Yudan Gezuri and spells out Rabbi Yehoshua ben Levi. Rabbi Yehoshua Buch’s Ohr LaYesharim reads the compressed chain as Yaakov citing Yudan, who cites Simon in the name of Yehoshua ben Levi, and tentatively associates Gezuri with Gezer.
